item.title: Australia: card surcharge reset
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Recheck checkout pricing: designated card-network surcharge rules changed. eftpos, Mastercard and Visa no-surcharge rules apply from 1 October after the RBA removed its prohibition on those rules. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/faqs/index.html

item.title: Domestic interchange: lower caps
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower domestic interchange caps make pass-through worth checking; net merchant savings depend on your terms. Revised interchange regulation applies to domestic-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Issuer compensation rules change
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check issuer incentives against the amended compensation rules. The amended net-compensation regime starts, with transitional arrangements for 2026/27. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Scheme fees come into view
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Use the new scheme-fee disclosures to challenge unexplained line items. First quarterly aggregate fee publications by designated card networks were due for the July–September period. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Acquirer fee disclosures begin
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Compare published acquirer fees with your own card mix and contract. Qualifying large acquirers must publish merchant service fee data by merchant size and card type. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Next: prove interchange pass-through
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your acquirer how the interchange reduction reached your statement. First publication of large acquirers’ interchange pass-through measures covers October–December 2026. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Foreign-issued cards get a cap
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review foreign-card pricing before the new caps apply. Interchange caps extend to foreign-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Merchant statements get sharper
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Make sure the new statement detail reaches your reconciliation process. More statement detail is required from the first full statement period starting on or after 1 April. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Scheme-fee roadmap expected
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Watch for the fee roadmap; it is not itself a price cap. The RBA expects a scheme-fee roadmap by 1 April; this is an expectation, not a new fee cap. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: NZ moves on commercial cards
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower regulated commercial-card interchange is coming; confirm what your acquirer passes through. The 22 October decision introduces commercial credit-card interchange limits on Mastercard and Visa. Official source: https://www.comcom.govt.nz/regulated-industries/projects/interchange-fee-regulation/

item.title: Same Day ACH: $10 million limit
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check whether the larger Same Day ACH limit changes your payout routing. Nacha lists an increase of the Same Day ACH dollar limit to $10 million for 17 September 2027. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH credits: 9am availability
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check payout promises against the receiving bank’s 9am availability duty. Non-Same Day ACH credits must be available by 9am in the receiving bank’s local time on settlement date. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/rules/funds-availability-requirements-non-same-day-credit-entries

item.title: ACH: IAT definition changes
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review how your ACH provider classifies international entries. Nacha lists its revised definition of International ACH Transactions among the September changes. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH availability exceptions update
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your bank which availability exceptions affect your credits. Nacha lists changes to funds-availability exceptions for Non-Same Day credit entries. Check the rule text before changing controls. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: IAT: optional date-of-birth field
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check how your IAT integration will handle the optional date-of-birth field. Nacha lists the optional date-of-birth field for IAT entries for 19 March 2027. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH: register IAT contacts
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Confirm ownership of IAT contact registration with your ACH provider. Registration of IAT contacts in the ACH Contact Registry is listed for 1 January 2027. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: UK scheme pricing: evidence required
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask for evidence behind relevant UK scheme-fee decisions, not a savings promise. Relevant scheme-fee decisions must comply with the PSR’s pricing-governance direction from the end of November. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/publications/policy-statements/ps261-market-review-of-card-scheme-and-processing-fees-final-decision-information-transparency-and-complexity-remedy-pricing-governance-remedy/

item.title: UK fee transparency: next stage
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Prepare to reconcile fee triggers with acquiring invoices. Substantive information, transparency and complexity requirements apply from the end of July 2027, subject to the limited fee-logic extension. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/publications/policy-statements/ps261-market-review-of-card-scheme-and-processing-fees-final-decision-information-transparency-and-complexity-remedy-pricing-governance-remedy/

item.title: Small fee lines: a limited extension
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Some fee logic arrives later; acquirers can request it during the extension. ITC Standard B is deferred for qualifying fee lines generating £850,000 or less in annual UK gross revenue. During the extension, acquirers can request that information without charge. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/media/nqoettxg/ps26-1-sp-fees-market-review-extensions-decision-aug-2026.pdf

item.title: Safeguarding: the operating baseline
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check how your provider reconciles and safeguards customer funds. Daily reconciliations, monthly reports and resolution packs form part of the strengthened safeguarding regime. Audit requirements have exceptions. Official source: https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/emi-payment-institutions-safeguarding-requirements

item.title: EU PSR: Council first-reading position
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Track the EU legislative process; this milestone is not an application date. The Council voting record documents adoption of its first-reading position on 29 October. This is a legislative milestone, not an application date. PSD3 and PSR must be tracked separately; no implementation date is asserted here. Official source: https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15154-2026-INIT/en/pdf

item.title: Canada: RTR launch set for 9 November
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check provider readiness for the scheduled RTR launch, not assumed availability. Payments Canada confirms a scheduled 9 November launch. This preview does not describe the service as already live. Official source: https://www.payments.ca/canadas-real-time-rail-launch-confirmed-budget-2026

item.title: PSD3: Council first-reading position
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Track PSD3 separately from PSR; do not treat this vote as a go-live date. The Council voting record documents its first-reading position on the payment and electronic-money services directive on 29 October. This is not an implementation deadline. Official source: https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15152-2026-INIT/en/pdf
